subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: Should OpenClaw expose a generic Gateway receipt timestamp to agent-visible inbound metadata, and if so what exact field name, timestamp representation, and propagation boundary should become the public contract?
rationale: The code proves the field is missing, but choosing `receivedAt` versus `gatewayReceivedAt`, ISO string versus epoch milliseconds, and the correct receive boundary is a cross-channel product/API decision rather than a narrow source bug.

options.title: Add one generic ingress timing contract
options.body: Expose a single additive field through the inbound event/template context and prompt metadata, backed by representative channel and SDK tests.

options.title: Keep receipt timing diagnostics-only
options.body: Rely on internal queues, OpenTelemetry, and channel-specific logs for latency attribution without adding agent-visible metadata.

options.title: Defer to channel-specific instrumentation
options.body: Leave the generic metadata unchanged and track receive-to-dispatch timing only in channel-specific latency issues such as LINE or iMessage.

recommendation.title: Add one generic ingress timing contract
recommendation.body: Expose a single additive field through the inbound event/template context and prompt metadata, backed by representative channel and SDK tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest historical ownership signal for the inbound prompt metadata surface where the public contract would land.
